### Observed differences

- The elapsed time between consecutive completion events of A24 followed by A17 roughly halved: in the earlier window these gaps averaged about 0.88 hours (about 53 minutes), with the middle half between about 0.80 and 0.99 hours, while in the later window they averaged about 0.43 hours (about 26 minutes), with the middle half between about 0.37 and 0.49 hours — a decrease of about 0.45 hours [TWAIT001].
- The gaps also became more uniform, with the standard deviation falling from about 0.13 to about 0.08 hours [TWAIT001].
- Slightly fewer such consecutive-pair gaps were observed: 56 before versus 48 after, in windows of 200 traces each [TWAIT001].
- The size of this difference is unusual for a random split of the pooled traces: it exceeds all but about 1 in 2,000 reference re-splits [TWAIT001].

### Inference

Support level: Insufficient evidence

The evidence is insufficient to infer a change in the process. Screening tested 54 time units and expected about 0.03 qualifying time items without a change (and about 0.33 control-flow items, none of which qualified), so a single qualifying item is what a stable process can still occasionally produce, and the apparent halving of the A24–A17 gap cannot be separated from sampling variation on this basis [TWAIT001].
